The '''Duchy of Ledostrov''' is a constitutional duchy in the northern/eastern political field of the Avant world. The old source often spells the country '''Ledestrov'''; this draft uses '''Ledostrov''' because that spelling appears in the source filename and map context, while preserving Ledestrov as an alias.

== Foundation ==

The duchy was founded in 840 when twenty-six nobles crowned the [[Count of Anavaisk]] as duke of the Ledostrov region. The early duchy survived through border skirmishes and diplomacy, incorporating several nearby states through negotiated means rather than large-scale conquest.

== Duma System ==

In 1352, after a period of ineffective rule, a noble council deposed the sitting duke and elevated the [[Prince of Novoanov]]. The [[Anavaisk-Novoanov Accords]] created the [[Duma of Ledostrov]], a body of landed nobles with power over war declarations, budgets, foreign treaties, and ducal elections.

The Duma system restrained ducal authority but also created long-term dependence on noble consensus. By the twentieth century, the source describes the Duma as increasingly corrupt, self-serving, and unable to pass essential budgets.

== Twentieth-Century Crisis ==

A famine in 1938 triggered a crisis after seven years of budget paralysis. The [[Burgrave of Sedava]], then duke, attempted to mobilize peasant support against the Duma in [[Novoanov]]. The military, aligned with the noble establishment, blocked him. Under the [[Count of Litwaldov]], Sedava's supporters were defeated at the [[Battle of Lisebev]]. Sedava was captured and executed for treason, and Litwaldov became duke.

Litwaldov suppressed smaller rebellions but died childless in 1942. The Duma failed to reach the required two-thirds majority for a new duke. A faction of five nobles led by [[Uzryta of Ledostrov|the Baron of Uzryta]] used military support to purge opponents and establish the [[Pentarchy of Ledostrov]].

== Reznikoff Reforms ==

After years of repression, protests, and army dissent, [[Reznikoff of Ledostrov]], commander of the [[Southern Defense Force of Ledostrov]], refused orders to suppress an uprising and marched on Novoanov. Uzryta was killed during the collapse of the Pentarchy, and Reznikoff declared himself duke.

Reznikoff expanded the Duma, added a popularly elected lower house, placed anti-corruption under ducal responsibility, and reorganized the military. By the 1994-back draft frame, these reforms explain how Ledostrov moved from noble paralysis and military-backed oligarchy toward a centralized reform duchy.

== Economy And Society ==

Ledostrov's economy combines heavy industry, arms production, machinery, textiles, consumer goods, and collective agriculture. The Pentarchy accelerated industrialization but worsened public hardship. Reznikoff's later economic reforms are described in 2003-era source wording, so this draft treats them as post-1994 trajectory unless separately confirmed.

Socially, Ledostrov remained hierarchical. Landed nobles, military officers, industrial managers, workers, and rural communities all shaped the post-Pentarchy order. The source also names [[Orderism]] as a rising Duma ideology, though the exact date and factional structure need review before publication.

== Source Limits ==

The source includes several 2003-era statements, including Reznikoff's age, succession worries, and selective engagement with AGGPI. This 1994-back draft preserves those as later trajectory notes only; it does not treat AGGPI engagement or the 2003 succession question as fixed pre-1995 facts.
